name: Question 7
problem:
Given the QR decomposition $A=QR,$ find the least-squares solution to $Ax=b,$ where

$$
Q=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}1 & \sqrt{2} \\ 2 & -\sqrt{2} \\ 1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}],\,R=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Substituting $A=QR,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ (QR)^{T}QRx & =(QR)^{T}b \\ {R}^{T}({Q}^{T}Q)Rx & ={R}^{T}{Q}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Q$ has orthonormal columns, ${Q}^{T}Q=I,$ and we get

$$
{R}^{T}Rx={R}^{T}\,{Q}^{T}b.
$$

Finally, since ${R}^{T}$ is invertible, pre-multiplying by $({R}^{T})^{-1}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}({R}^{T})^{-1}\cdot {R}^{T}Rx & =({R}^{T})^{-1}\cdot {R}^{T}{Q}^{T}b \\ Rx & ={Q}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting our matrices, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}x & =\overset{{Q}^{T}}{\overset{⏞}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ \sqrt{2} & -\sqrt{2} & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}} \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]x & =[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=20 \\ 2\sqrt{2}{x}_{2}=-4\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-(-2) & =20 \\ 2{x}_{1} & =18 \\ {x}_{1} & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the least-squares solution to $Ax=b$ is $[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Question 7
?

Given the QR decomposition A=QR, find the least-squares solution to Ax=b, where Q=16[122−212],R=16[2−1022],b=[282].

a
[−32]
b
[23]
c
[3−2]
d
[9−2]
e
[92]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The least-squares solution of Ax=b satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

ATAx=ATb

Substituting A=QR, we obtain

ATAx=ATb(QR)TQRx=(QR)TbRT(QTQ)Rx=RTQTb.

Since Q has orthonormal columns, QTQ=I, and we get

RTRx=RTQTb.

Finally, since RT is invertible, pre-multiplying by (RT)−1 gives

(RT)−1⋅RTRx=(RT)−1⋅RTQTbRx=QTb.

Now, substituting our matrices, we have

16[2−1022]⏞Rx=16[1212−22]⏞QT[282]⏞b[2−1022]x=[20−42]

which gives the system

{2x1−x2=2022x2=−42.

From the second equation, we get x2=−2. Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

2x1−(−2)=202x1=18x1=9.

Therefore, the least-squares solution to Ax=b is [9−2].
